previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic graft-versus-host disease, prior stem cell transplant, and history of venous thromboembolism was admitted after worsening chest pain following a motor vehicle accident three days prior. Imaging revealed an acute sternal fracture and an acute left 6th rib fracture, with no evidence of intrathoracic injury. She was admitted for pain control and monitoring. Pain was initially managed with oxycodone and a lidocaine patch, then transitioned to hydromorphone (Dilaudid) for better control. She remained hemodynamically stable, afebrile, and was able to ambulate and tolerate oral intake. Incentive spirometry was used to prevent pulmonary complications. She was discharged home with services on hospital day 3 with a pain regimen including acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and PRN hydromorphone, along with continued enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with fever, hypotension, abdominal pain. 
Evaluate for evidence of infection or other source of fevers.

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  CTDIvol: 29.54 mGy
DLP: 529.77 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  ___ ___
CT abdomen and pelvis ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There is mild dependent atelectasis in the bilateral lower lobes.
There is a calcified left hilar lymph node.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. There
is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation. The gallbladder is surgically absent.

PANCREAS: There is a rounded hypoattenuated focus measuring 1.9 x 1.5 cm in
the region the pancreatic head (02:31) which previously was characterized as a
pancreatic cystic lesion on MRCP ___.  Other subcentimeter T2 cystic
foci noted on ___ ___ are poorly delineated on this study.  There is
no main ductal dilatation.  Is mild fatty atrophy of the pancreas.

SPLEEN: There are two rounded hypoattenuated foci measuring 1.7 and 1.1 cm
(2:9 and 13), respectively, likely representing epithelial cysts, previously
characterized on MRCP ___.  The spleen is normal in size.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram.
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable. Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  There is wall
thickening with associated diverticula in the sigmoid colon and adjacent mild
fatty stranding.  The appendix is normal.  There is no evidence of
obstruction.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus is unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy. There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: Compression deformities of the T11 and L1 vertebral bodies are
unchanged as compared to CT abdomen and pelvis ___.  There are
moderate degenerative changes of the bilateral hips.  There is no evidence of
worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: Irregular intermediate density rounded foci in the subcutaneous
tissues of the anterior abdominal wall likely represents sequelae of
subcutaneous injections.

IMPRESSION:


1. Wall thickening with mild pericolonic fat  stranding surrounding a focal
segment of the  sigmoid colon in the region of multiple diverticula, without
evidence of abscess or extraperitoneal air, is compatible with acute
uncomplicated sigmoid colonic diverticulitis.
2. Stable rounded hypo-attenuated lesion measuring 1.9 cm in the pancreatic
head corresponded to a pancreatic cystic lesion likely a side-branch IPMN
noted on MRCP ___.
3. Chronic compression fractures of the T11 and L1 vertebral bodies are
unchanged from CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen pelvis

INDICATION:  ___ w/ CML in remission, hypogammaglobulinemia on IVIG, h/oGVHD
on chronic prednisone, SIBO, DVT/PE on lovenox, DM2, who was admitted with abd
pain and hypotension, found to have sigmoid diverticulitis, complicated by
hypotension briefly requiring pressors now improved, now found to have
Salmonella gastroenteritis.// Abdomen distended and still having pain. Assess
for ascites or worsening diverticulitis

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 464 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis ___
MRCP ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Lung bases are clear.  No pleural effusion.  Trace pericardial
fluid is likely physiologic.

ABDOMEN:
HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is surgically absent.

PANCREAS: There is fatty atrophy of the pancreatic head.  There is a 2.5 cm
cystic lesion arising from the pancreatic head, unchanged, and better assessed
on recent MRCP.  No pancreatic ductal dilation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: 1.7 and 1.0 cm hypodense lesions in the spleen are unchanged, likely
representing cysts.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  Subcentimeter
hypodensity in the upper pole of the right kidney is too small to
characterize, but likely represent simple cysts.  There is no perinephric
abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Previously seen
mild fat stranding surrounding focal segment of the sigmoid colon appears
resolved.  Multiple sigmoid diverticula are again noted.  Areas of mild wall
thickening in the sigmoid colon is suggestive of chronic diverticular changes
(5:67).  No evidence of active colitis.  The appendix is normal.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Uterus is unremarkable.  No adnexal abnormalities are
seen.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Compression deformities of the L1 and T11 vertebral bodies are unchanged from
prior exam.

SOFT TISSUES: A coarse calcification is noted in the right breast.  Multiple
injection granulomas noted in the subcutaneous fat of the low anterior
abdomen.  Small foci of subcutaneous gas are also likely related to
injections.


IMPRESSION:


1. Interval resolution of mild fat stranding previously seen around the
sigmoid colon suggesting resolution of episode of acute diverticulitis.  Mild
sigmoid colonic wall thickening likely reflect changes from chronic
diverticular disease.
2. Stable 2.5 cm cystic lesion in the pancreatic head better characterized on
recent MRCP.
